query: Why do the service discovery refresh failure metrics vanish after reloading the config, until Prometheus is restarted?

keyFacts.fact: A reload deleted the per-job prometheus_sd_refresh_* series even though a discovery provider for that job was still running; the bug came from #17614.
It happens when a job's discovery settings change (for example the http_sd url) or the job is renamed, and the series only come back after a restart.

PR #19878 fixes it: providers remember the job name they were created for, and a reload deletes refresh metrics only for cancelled providers with no other running provider of the same mechanism and job.

query: Should samples produced by a subquery be counted again in the TotalSamples query statistic?

keyFacts.fact: PR #19165 counted the samples processed inside a subquery in the parent's TotalSamples, which previously under-reported subquery work.
Reviewers objected that also counting the subquery's materialized output is inconsistent with range vector selectors, whose function output is not counted.
PR #19873, from a maintainer, proposes not counting materialized subquery points again, because inner consumption is already merged into the parent and vector selectors are not charged either.
The discussion does not show a final merged decision.

query: The template helper that strips domain names cuts IPv6 addresses whose interface zone contains a dot

keyFacts.fact: stripDomain used net.ParseIP, which rejects addresses with a zone identifier, so such addresses were treated as hostnames and cut at the first dot (fe80::1%eth0.100 became fe80::1%eth0).
PR #19908 switches the check to netip.ParseAddr, which accepts zones; hostname handling is unchanged.

query: What happens when BucketFraction gets an empty bucket list?

keyFacts.fact: It panics with index out of range [-1] for a nil or empty slice, because it reads the last bucket before checking the length.
PR #19944 makes it return NaN for nil and empty slices, mirroring the BucketQuantile fix (#19927).
The PromQL caller already skips empty bucket lists, so no query crash was demonstrated.

query: Why did the BucketQuantile empty-slice fix not claim any user-facing PromQL failure?

keyFacts.fact: Current PromQL call sites already guard against empty bucket inputs, so the panic affected only the exported helper's contract, not query evaluation.
The fix returns NaN for nil and empty slices, as the helper already documented for fewer than two buckets.

query: How were the OpenMetrics 2.0 parser follow-up items split across pull requests to keep reviews small?

keyFacts.fact: The work was split into three PRs of roughly 200-300 lines: numeric validation items 6, 7 and 8 (#19746); lexer, label, exemplar, metadata and option items 1-5, 9-11 and 13 (#19748); and zero-allocation parsing item 12 (#19747).
Items 6, 7 and 8 were grouped because they are the same kind of bug in the composite value parsing path.
Field-order enforcement (item 14) was split out of #19747 to keep that PR limited to performance with no behaviour change.

query: A negative histogram count in the OM2 text parser ends up as an enormous unsigned number

keyFacts.fact: A negative count or zero_count is cast to uint64 in buildNativeHistogram and wraps around, for example -5 becomes 18446744073709551611.
The tracking issue lists it as item 6: validate count and zero_count are non-negative before the cast; gauge gcount hits the same cast.

query: Proposal to let operators correct a metric's type, unit and help text instead of trusting the exporter

keyFacts.fact: Issue #19832 proposes letting operators rewrite TYPE, UNIT and HELP metadata, which today cannot be changed while labels can be relabelled freely.

It matters because with type-and-unit labels, metadata becomes part of series identity and PromQL behaviour; use cases include untyped exporters, missing units, OTLP/remote-write parity and huge HELP strings.
The suggested direction is option A (post-relabel __type__/__unit__ are authoritative) plus option B (a family-level metadata_relabel_configs stage for HELP).
It is still a request for feedback, not a decided design.

query: What are the drawbacks of fixing metadata by relabeling __type__ and __unit__?

keyFacts.fact: The metadata record never sees relabelling, so series labels, the metadata WAL record and /api/v1/metadata can disagree.
Type set per series clashes with family-level metadata: one part of a classic histogram family can get a different __type__ than the others.
HELP has no label form, so it cannot be set or dropped this way.
Type and unit values are not validated (typos like guage are accepted) and the change does not reach the OTLP or remote-write receive paths.
Renaming a metric through relabelling silently drops its metadata.

query: Has the NHCBParser start timestamp optimisation been completed, and which pull requests did it?

keyFacts.fact: Yes, it is done.
#19446 calls StartTimestamp() only when start-timestamp parsing is requested; #17156 makes the protobuf parser convert to NHCB directly; #19880 does the same for the OM2 parser (39-63% less CPU).
The relabel fast path #18327 is still open.

query: Docker Swarm discovery never fills container labels; is an extra API call per task acceptable?

keyFacts.fact: The Swarm tasks API returns empty container labels, so __meta_dockerswarm_container_label_* never populates; PR #19284 adds a container inspect call per task to fill them.
The cost is one extra Docker API call per task per refresh, and docker-socket-proxy setups need inspect permission; the author asked whether it should be opt-in.
No maintainer decision on the cost appears in the discussion.

query: Replacing removed labels with a whole-series hash could hide duplicate label set errors in queries

keyFacts.fact: If a query destroys the distinguishing label (for example with label_replace), it should fail with 'vector cannot contain metrics with the same labelset', but a whole-series hash keeps the series distinct and hides that error.
The suggested alternative is to hash only the removed labels, so duplicates are still detected.
The PR author says his engine avoids the problem by checking the original hash only when labels collide after removal.

query: Why keep the original labels hash as an integer rather than encoding it into a label?

keyFacts.fact: The hash is already stored as a uint64; encoding it as a label string wastes bytes even with base-91 style encodings.
Comparing uint64 values is much faster than comparing strings, a large gain for Thanos deduplicating millions of series.
The trade-off is extra code and a hole in the everything-is-a-label model.

query: OTel histograms with an explicit infinite bucket boundary write the +Inf bucket twice

keyFacts.fact: The OTel SDK accepts +Inf as an explicit bound, and the translator then wrote le="+Inf" twice for the same series and timestamp: once from the bounds loop and once synthesized from the count.
PR #19425 skips the infinite bound in the loop, lets the count carry the +Inf bucket, and emits a warning.

query: Should the OTLP translator reject an explicit +Inf bound like the NHCB path does, or just warn?

keyFacts.fact: The PR normalizes the +Inf bound and warns instead of rejecting, so the histogram keeps flowing and no already-written sample changes.
The warning was added because the NHCB path rejects an explicit +Inf bound, and silently repairing it would be inconsistent.
The author left reject-versus-warn to the maintainers; no decision is recorded.

query: A test fixture whose histogram count does not match the sum of its bucket counts

keyFacts.fact: TestFromMetrics' histogram_1 fixture had count 15 but bucket counts 3, 11, 0 summing to 14; the sum of 155 showed one observation belonged in the overflow bucket, which was set to 1.
Expected native histograms in that block are now checked with Validate so a non-conforming fixture fails the test.
The TestTemporality exponential fixtures were also invalid: count 1 with no buckets.

query: Were the TestTemporality exponential histogram fixtures with no buckets intentional?

keyFacts.fact: No; the maintainer said it did not look deliberate.
Commit a89fd357b added a minimal bucket to those fixtures and the same Validate check.

query: Should the promtool lint about scrape interval and lookback delta also include the scrape timeout?

keyFacts.fact: PR #19911 proposes flagging scrape_interval + scrape_timeout >= lookback_delta, because a slow scrape can let the up series disappear and reset alert state.
The maintainer was sceptical: samples are stamped at scrape start so such configurations can be valid, and a lint should flag only problems fixable with a simple change.
No decision to change the lint is recorded.

query: Is there a command to scan stored data for classic histograms whose buckets contradict each other?

keyFacts.fact: Yes: an experimental promtool tsdb check-histograms command, added in PR #19427.
It reports non-monotonic buckets, le="+Inf" disagreeing with _count, unparsable le values, conflicting duplicate le spellings and missing +Inf buckets, and exits non-zero on findings.
Native histograms are out of scope because they are validated at append.

query: promtool series and label queries cannot be used with tenant headers

keyFacts.fact: promtool query series and query labels did not pass custom headers, so header-based multi-tenancy such as X-Scope-OrgID did not work.
PR #19335 adds --header to both commands.

query: Exemplars disappear after compaction followed by a restart

keyFacts.fact: Exemplars are not stored in blocks and are recovered from WAL replay; compaction could drop a series identity while its exemplar record remained, so the exemplar was lost on restart.
PR #19940 keeps a series identity until its latest exemplar falls below the replay cutoff.

query: Restoring from a memory snapshot forgets when series references expire

keyFacts.fact: Snapshot recovery lost expiry timestamps for series references no longer in the head, so a later checkpoint could drop series records that retained samples need.
PR #19590 persists expiries in snapshot records and restores them before WAL replay; older snapshots fall back to full WAL replay.

query: What breaking effects came with upgrading the Go client library to 1.25?

keyFacts.fact: Query, QueryRange, Series, LabelNames and LabelValues now return Infos annotations in addition to Warnings.
client_golang now requires Go 1.26.
It also bumps prometheus/common to v0.72.0 and procfs to v0.22.0.

query: Discovering Amazon managed RabbitMQ brokers as scrape targets

keyFacts.fact: PR #19750 adds an MQ role to AWS service discovery for Amazon MQ (RabbitMQ and ActiveMQ).
RabbitMQ on Amazon MQ now exposes Prometheus metrics, so brokers can be discovered without a third-party discovery service or hard-coded targets.

query: Printing inf ^ 2 gives a query that parses back with a different meaning

keyFacts.fact: ^ binds tighter than a unary sign, and Inf prints as +Inf, so inf ^ 2 printed as +Inf ^ 2, which parses back as +(Inf ^ 2).
PR #19821 puts a signed left operand of ^ in parentheses, printing (+Inf) ^ 2; the web UI fix is #19823.

query: group_right swaps operands but the fill defaults stay on the wrong side

keyFacts.fact: group_right swaps operands internally but did not swap the fill defaults, so fill_left/fill_right filled the wrong side (giving 1 and 25 instead of -1 and 23 in the example).
PR #19939 swaps the fill pointers together with the vectors.

query: Handling queries during a migration where both classic and custom-bucket native histograms exist for one metric

keyFacts.fact: PR #19881 groups stored classic and converted NHCB series by histogram identity, and at timestamps where a classic sample exists it shadows the converted NHCB samples to avoid duplicate buckets.
Disjoint time ranges across a migration cutover are merged into one continuous series, preferring live samples over staleness markers.
The PR is a draft chained on #18048.

query: Moving the remote write receiver to the new appender interface

keyFacts.fact: PR #19812 migrates the Remote Write 1.0 and 2.x receiver to AppenderV2 and requires ExemplarAppenderV2, returning HTTP 500 if it is unsupported.
It is an alternative to #19457.

query: Does DNS service discovery resolve .local multicast names?

keyFacts.fact: No, dns_sd_config does not resolve mDNS names; the planned change only documents this and adds a test, without implementing mDNS.

query: Created timestamp is ignored when the _created line lists labels in a different order

keyFacts.fact: The start timestamp lookup keyed on the source label order, so a _created line with labels in a different order returned 0.
PR #19942 sorts the label pairs before hashing.

query: Exporters that sort histogram lines alphabetically break conversion to native histograms

keyFacts.fact: NHCBParser expects all series of one classic histogram to be contiguous; alphabetically sorted output produces incomplete histograms and drops _sum lines.
That ordering is allowed by the Prometheus text format but forbidden by OpenMetrics.
It is a known issue left unfixed because a fix adds overhead for a niche case; PR #19050 only adds a test documenting it.

query: Should delta-to-cumulative conversion for OTLP be deprecated or removed right away?

keyFacts.fact: There are two competing PRs: #19950 deprecates the otlp-deltatocumulative flag with a warning, and #19951 removes it immediately.
Only one will be merged after maintainer discussion; it is not decided.
A maintainer's first reaction was that removal would probably have to wait for Prometheus 4.0.

query: Rule unit tests cannot repeat NaN or stale values with the x notation

keyFacts.fact: The lexer read NaNx3, Infx3 and stalex3 as a single identifier, so they failed to parse.
PR #19972 makes Inf, NaN and stale stop before a following x, so stalex3 and NaNx4 work in test series.

query: histogram_quantile picks the wrong bucket when the histogram sum is NaN

keyFacts.fact: When a native histogram's sum is NaN, the scan for NaN observations overwrote the selected bucket, so interpolation used the last bucket (about 3.03 instead of 1.52 in the example).
PR #19973 preserves the selected bucket.

query: Plan to switch Prometheus's own internal summaries to native histograms

keyFacts.fact: Issue #19976 proposes migrating all remaining internal Summary and Histogram metrics to native histograms.
The issue is a one-line proposal with no further detail or timeline.
